# # Map customer React Suspense boundary unmount on Relay store invalidation to the React reconciler / Relay environment boundary

A customer reports that their React 18 + Relay 16 page silently unmounts
and remounts a Suspense boundary every time a Relay store invalidation
fires from a mutation, even though no fragment subscribed to that
boundary actually reads the invalidated record. The whole subtree's
client-side state is lost.

Your task:
1. Find where React's reconciler decides whether a Suspense boundary
   re-renders or unmounts after a context update.
2. Find where Relay's RelayModernEnvironment publishes a store
   invalidation and how it notifies subscribers via
   useSubscribeToInvalidationState.
3. Trace the cross-repo path: Relay store mutation commit ->
   notify subscribers -> useFragment / useLazyLoadQuery hook re-eval
   -> React useSyncExternalStore subscription -> reconciler
   schedules update -> Suspense boundary re-render decision. Cite
   each file and the function or attribute responsible.
4. Identify why a global store-version bump can transitively cause
   any consumer of useFragment under the Suspense boundary to
   re-throw a promise, forcing the boundary to fall back.


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/react--v18.2.0, github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0

Here is the complete cross-repo trace, citing every file and responsible function/attribute.

---

## 1. React reconciler: how a Suspense boundary decides to unmount vs. re-render

The decision happens in three coordinated phases:

### a. Throw detection — `throwException`
[`ReactFiberThrow.new.js:405`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/react--v18.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberThrow.new.js?L405-L494)

When any component throws a Promise (a "wakeable") during render, `throwException` is called. It:
1. Marks the source fiber `Incomplete`.
2. Calls `getNearestSuspenseBoundaryToCapture` ([L272](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/react--v18.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberThrow.new.js?L272)) to walk up the fiber tree and find the nearest `SuspenseComponent` fiber that `shouldCaptureSuspense`.
3. Calls `markSuspenseBoundaryShouldCapture` ([L292](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/react--v18.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberThrow.new.js?L292)), which in concurrent mode sets `suspenseBoundary.flags |= ShouldCapture` ([L398](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/react--v18.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberThrow.new.js?L398)).

### b. Unwind — `unwindWork` on `SuspenseComponent`
[`ReactFiberUnwindWork.new.js:105`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/react--v18.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberUnwindWork.new.js?L105-L131)

As the work loop unwinds up the fiber tree, it finds the boundary with `ShouldCapture` and **converts it to `DidCapture`** (`flags = (flags & ~ShouldCapture) | DidCapture`, L121). This causes the boundary to restart its render with `didSuspend = true`.

### c. Fallback render — `updateSuspenseComponent`
[`ReactFiberBeginWork.new.js:2143`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/react--v18.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberBeginWork.new.js?L2143-L2165)

On re-entry, the boundary reads `didSuspend` (derived from `DidCapture` on `workInProgress.flags`). When `showFallback` is true, it calls `updateSuspenseFallbackChildren`, which renders the fallback and **hides (unmounts) the primary subtree** via the `Offscreen` fiber with `hidden` mode. All client-side state in the primary tree is lost.

---

## 2. Relay store invalidation and subscriber notification

### a. Mutation commit → publish
`environment.commitUpdate(updater)` ([`RelayModernEnvironment.js:254`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayModernEnvironment.js?L254-L258)) enqueues the updater and calls `_publishQueue.run()`.

### b. `RelayPublishQueue.run()`
[`RelayPublishQueue.js:209`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayPublishQueue.js?L209-L273)

1. Calls `_commitData()` ([L333](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayPublishQueue.js?L333)), which runs each pending updater through a `RelayRecordSourceProxy`.
2. If the updater calls `storeProxy.invalidateStore()`, the proxy marks itself, and `recordSourceProxy.isStoreMarkedForInvalidation()` returns `true` → `invalidatedStore = true`.
3. After all data is committed, returns `this._store.notify(sourceOperation, invalidatedStore)` ([L273](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayPublishQueue.js?L273)).

### c. `RelayModernStore.notify()`
[`RelayModernStore.js:307`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayModernStore.js?L307-L393)

Two critical things happen:

1. **Global epoch bump** ([L321-L324](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayModernStore.js?L321-L324)):
   ```js
   this._currentWriteEpoch++;
   if (invalidateStore === true) {
     this._globalInvalidationEpoch = this._currentWriteEpoch;
   }
   ```

2. **Invalidation subscribers notified** ([L342-L347](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayModernStore.js?L342-L347)):
   ```js
   this._invalidationSubscriptions.forEach(subscription => {
     this._updateInvalidationSubscription(subscription, invalidateStore === true);
   });
   ```

### d. `_updateInvalidationSubscription`
[`RelayModernStore.js:510-523`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayModernStore.js?L510-L523)

```js
const isSubscribedToInvalidatedIDs =
  invalidatedStore ||   // <-- GLOBAL: fires for ALL subscribers when invalidatedStore=true
  dataIDs.some(dataID => this._invalidatedRecordIDs.has(dataID));
if (!isSubscribedToInvalidatedIDs) { return; }
callback();
```

**When `invalidatedStore` is `true`, every registered invalidation subscriber fires, regardless of whether it cares about the invalidated records.**

### e. `useSubscribeToInvalidationState`
[`useSubscribeToInvalidationState.js:28`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-relay/relay-hooks/useSubscribeToInvalidationState.js?L28-L57)

This hook registers a callback via `store.subscribeToInvalidationState`. That callback fires unconditionally on a global invalidation.

## 4. Why a global store-version bump can force any `useFragment` consumer to re-throw a promise

This is the root cause of the customer's bug, and it involves two compounding mechanisms:

### Mechanism A: `_globalInvalidationEpoch` causes `isMissingData` on every retained query

When `notify(op, invalidatedStore=true)` runs, `_globalInvalidationEpoch` is set to `_currentWriteEpoch` ([`RelayModernStore.js:324`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayModernStore.js?L324)). The `lookupInvalidationState` function always includes `'global'` in its invalidation map ([L467](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayModernStore.js?L467)):

```js
invalidations.set('global', this._globalInvalidationEpoch);
```

This means `checkInvalidationState` ([L474](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/relay-runtime/store/RelayModernStore.js?L474)) returns `true` for **every** retained operation — the entire store is considered stale. When `check()` re-evaluates these operations, it may find that some data that was previously "available" is now marked as invalidated, producing `isMissingData = true` on the resulting snapshots.

### Mechanism B: `isMissingData` causes `FragmentResource.readWithIdentifier` to look for an in-flight request and throw

In [`FragmentResource.js:378-499`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-relay/relay-hooks/legacy/FragmentResource.js?L378-L499), if a fresh snapshot has `isMissingData = true`, the code checks for a pending parent query via `_getAndSavePromiseForFragmentRequestInFlight`. If **any** refetch or revalidation request is in flight at this moment (which is common after a mutation that triggers a refetchQuery), that promise is stored in the cache as `kind: 'pending'` and then **thrown**.

### Mechanism C: Stale cache entry with `kind: 'pending'` throws for all readers

Once a cache entry is `kind: 'pending'` ([`FragmentResource.js:294-304`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/relay--v16.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-relay/relay-hooks/legacy/FragmentResource.js?L294-L304)):
```js
if (cachedValue.kind === 'pending' && isPromise(cachedValue.promise)) {
  throw cachedValue.promise;
}
```
Every component that reads the same `fragmentIdentifier` during this render pass will throw this cached promise — even components whose fragments **did not read any of the invalidated records**. The `fragmentIdentifier` is keyed by fragment + owner variables, not by the specific record IDs that changed.

### The combined effect

A global invalidation from `storeProxy.invalidateStore()` (or any mutation that sets the flag):
1. Bumps `_globalInvalidationEpoch`, marking every retained query stale.
2. Fires **every** `_invalidationSubscription` callback unconditionally.
3. Forces each fragment component to re-render (via `forceUpdate`).
4. During re-render, if any related network request is in-flight (the refetch triggered by the mutation), `readWithIdentifier` throws a Promise regardless of whether this specific fragment's data changed.
5. React's `throwException` → `markSuspenseBoundaryShouldCapture` → `unwindWork` → `DidCapture` path causes the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary to swap to its fallback, unmounting the entire primary subtree and destroying all client-side state.

The fix is to **not use `invalidateStore()` globally** for targeted mutations. Instead, invalidate only the specific record IDs via `store.get(id).invalidateRecord()`, so `_updateInvalidationSubscription` only fires for subscriptions that actually include those IDs, and the `isMissingData` surface area stays narrow.
